main_text.p: accurata [?]inspicerem, num dictiones illæ absqve mendis essent exaratæ. Verùm cum alioqvin homo ille sit solers atqve in his rebus admodum versatus, facile in suspicionem incidi, ne forte dictiones illæ nullum hujusmodi patiantur defe-ctum, sed peculiari qvodam modo Samaritani idiomatis ita se habeant; Lin-gvam enim Samaritanam, etsi ex Hebrai-ca & Chaldaica ortum ducit, mixtione tamen, & proprio ipsius Samaritanismo, in tertium qvid ab ambobus diversum, degenerasse arbitror. Dictiones vero Chaldæis & Syris tantopere insolentes, non absurde suspicari licet, Arabicas es-se: nam ab Arabismis non puto Samari-tanos abhorrere, qvippe qvi hodie Ara-bico sermone pro vulgari utuntur. Si voces istas ad me transmisisses, & loca, un-de excerpta erant adnotasses, facile in textu meo Samaritano, qvomodo se ha-beant, comperissem. Versiculum 15. tertii capitis Exodi, ubi de nomine in-effabili verba habentur, in codice meo Samaritano reperi qvidem, aliqvo tamen

page.notes: Printed "inspicerem" is partly damaged at the start of the first line; read as "inspicerem" from the context of the sentence, marked [?]. Versiculum is printed with a long s. Some letters on the right side of the lines are faint from the scan.
